title: FlexPipe: Maximizing Training Efficiency for Transformer-based Models with Variable-Length Inputs
problem: Training transformers with variable-length inputs causes padding waste and pipeline stage imbalances. GPU hardware cannot efficiently handle heterogeneous sequence lengths within a single batch.
motivation: Variable-length input sequences are ubiquitous in NLP, but current pipeline-parallel training wastes computation on padding tokens and suffers from load imbalance across pipeline stages.
method: FlexPipe groups sequences by actual length instead of padding them to uniform length. It then dynamically reconfigures the pipeline—the parallel stages that process data on the GPU—to match these groups. This eliminates wasted computation from padding while keeping all pipeline stages active and busy.
key_novelty: Dynamically adjust the pipeline to match how input lengths are actually distributed, rather than enforcing fixed-length batching and padding.
contributions: Flexible pipeline architecture for variable-length transformer training
Dynamic length-aware batching strategy to reduce padding waste
Pipeline stage scheduling optimized for heterogeneous sequence lengths
Demonstration of improved training throughput on GPU infrastructure
